text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargeFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: John.

Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others to their ceremony make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → ∃y Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others to their ceremony.
∀x (LargeFamily(x) → (WellAttendedWedding(x) ∨ ∃y Invite(x, y))) ::: People with larger families have well-attended weddings or invite friends.
Engaged(John) ::: John is engaged.
¬Invite(John, y) ∧ ¬WeddingPlans(John) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and does not make wedding plans.
LargeFamily(John) → (WellAttendedWedding(John) ∨ ∃y Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.

Conclusion:
¬LargeFamily(John) ::: John does not have a larger family.
